paper_metadata.title: Software for Creating Scalable Benchmarks from Quantum Algorithms

summary: The paper introduces the scarab benchmarking tool (implemented in pyGSTi 0.9.14) for scalable estimation of quantum circuit process fidelity using mirror‑circuit fidelity estimation. Experiments include simulations up to 10,000‑qubit circuits for benchmarking runtime scaling, Hamiltonian‑simulation benchmark circuits up to 10 qubits, and hardware demonstrations on IBM Kingston and IBM Fez with circuits up to ~10 qubits. The method estimates circuit process fidelity using proxy mirror circuits with sampling parameters such as |M1|=|M2|=|M3| up to 1000 and demonstrates accurate fidelity estimation across multiple noise models.

experiments.description: Simulation study validating scarab fidelity estimation using QFT and QPE circuits under multiple noise models.

algorithm.variant: QFT and QPE circuits used as benchmarking targets

key_results: Circuits from 3–6 qubits simulated.
MCFE parameters |M1| = |M2| = |M3| = 1000.
Estimated process fidelity from scarab closely matches true process fidelity across depolarizing, readout, coherent idle rotation, and combined noise models (Fig. 3).

experiments.description: Runtime scaling evaluation of the scarab benchmark generation pipeline.

algorithm.variant: benchmark generation for U3–CZ brickwork circuits

key_results: Test circuits: depth‑128 U3‑CZ brickwork circuits.
Low-level and subcircuit benchmarks tested up to 10,000 qubits.
Classical preprocessing time tc scales approximately linearly for low-level benchmarks and sublinearly for subcircuit benchmarks.
Full‑stack benchmark runtime tested up to 150 qubits using IBM Fez transpilation.

experiments.description: Simulation of Hamiltonian‑simulation benchmarks using HamLib Hamiltonians to validate fidelity decomposition and scaling.
key_results: First‑order Trotter circuits for TFIM, Heisenberg, Bose‑Hubbard, and Fermi‑Hubbard Hamiltonians.
Circuit sizes from 2–10 qubits.
Noise model includes depolarizing noise (λ1Q=0.0005, λ2Q=0.005), coherent over‑rotations (0.01 rad), and readout error (ε=0.01).
Scarab estimates of noise process fidelity closely match exact values for n≤6 qubits (Fig. 4).

experiments.description: Full‑stack compilation benchmark for QAOA circuits evaluating approximate compilation on IBM Fez.

algorithm.variant: p=1 QAOA with random GNP(n, 2 ln(n)/n) graphs

key_results: Circuits from 2–10 qubits.
Approximation_degree varied from 0.9 to 1.0 in Qiskit transpiler.
10 stochastic transpilation runs per circuit.
Process fidelity generally highest at approximation_degree=1.0 except for larger QFT cases where dropping small rotations improved fidelity.
